proposal.original_claim_summary: The entry centers on an independent estimate of nearly $115 million in second-term Trump golf travel/security costs and a $300 million end-of-term projection, while also stating that Trump spent 191 of his first 512 days at his properties.

identified_problems.explanation: The $115 million cumulative cost and $300 million projection are not supported by a GAO, Secret Service, congressional accounting, or another comparably auditable official source located in this review.
The headline presents an independent tracker estimate as a settled taxpayer-cost figure.
The 191-of-512-days / 37% property-visit statistic is independently documented by CREW, but it does not validate the dollar estimates.

proposal.proposed_synopsis: A June 2026 CREW analysis reported that Trump had visited properties he owns on 191 of his first 512 days back in office, or 37% of the time. Independent websites have estimated golf-related travel costs, but the specific $115 million cumulative cost and $300 million projection were not verified against an authoritative government accounting source. The current cost-centered record should be hidden pending auditable sourcing or replaced with a separately sourced property-visit record.

frozen_original.title: Trump Golf Trips Top 115 Million in Taxpayer Costs on Track for 300 Million by End of Term
frozen_original.synopsis: By August 2026, independent tracker estimates put Trumps second-term golf-related travel and security costs at nearly 115 million dollars, including 80 million for 59 days at Mar-a-Lago and 13.6 million for Bedminster. Trump visited his own properties on 191 of his first 512 days in office, or 37 percent of the time. At his pace the tracker projects 300 million total by end of term, doubling his first-term total.

proposal.original_claim_summary: Trump Administration Creates 'Disloyal' Federal Employee List for Termination
proposal.original_synopsis: The Trump administration compiled lists of federal employees identified as politically 'disloyal' based on social media posts, donation history, and internal reporting by coworkers, with the intent to terminate them under Schedule F. The lists were reportedly compiled with help from DOGE operatives who accessed personnel databases across multiple agencies. Whistleblowers described an atmosphere of fear in which employees were afraid to communicate internally lest any comment be construed as disloyalty. Civil service experts warned the lists represented a return to McCarthyite political purges of the federal workforce. Several lawsuits challenged the legality of terminating employees based on political affiliation.

frozen_original.title: Trump Threatens Columbia University Funding Over Gaza Protests
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, the Trump administration threatened to cut $400 million in federal funding to Columbia University over the university's handling of pro-Palestinian protests on campus in 2024, demanding that Columbia adopt new disciplinary policies, restructure its Middle East studies department under federal oversight, and report student protesters to law enforcement. The demands were accompanied by explicit threats of criminal prosecution of university administrators. Columbia's board and interim president faced intense pressure from both the administration and donors. Legal experts called the demands an unconstitutional federal takeover of a private university's internal affairs. The episode was part of a coordinated campaign targeting elite universities the administration accused of harboring antisemitism and radical ideology.

frozen_original.title: Trump Executive Order Forcing States to Defund Planned Parenthood
frozen_original.synopsis: In February 2025, the Trump administration issued executive orders and Medicaid guidance directing states to exclude Planned Parenthood and other abortion providers from their Medicaid programs as a condition of receiving federal Medicaid funding, even though federal law has long required Medicaid to cover services from any qualified provider. Planned Parenthood serves approximately 2.4 million patients per year through Medicaid, the vast majority of whom receive services entirely unrelated to abortion — including cancer screenings, STI testing, contraception, and well-woman exams. Multiple federal courts had previously blocked similar state-level efforts to exclude Planned Parenthood from Medicaid, ruling they violated federal law. The directive was projected to eliminate healthcare access for millions of low-income patients who had no alternative provider in their area.
